To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the EU has shifted from a general entrepreneurial focus to a more focused focus on innovation; (2) this shift has been accompanied by a shift from a general focus on learning to a more focused research focus; (3) this shift has brought about a shift in the way that the university is imagined and in the role of the researcher; and (4) this shift has had an impact on the way that the researcher is imagined and on the role of the research itself.

1. the shift to innovation as a policy priority is a shift in emphasis from a generalised entrepreneurialism to a specific focus on innovation, 2. the shift is accompanied by a shift from learning to research and from the individual researcher to the innovative researcher, and 3. this shift is accompanied by shifts in the nature of critique, from critique to research and from critique as a mode of resistance to research as a mode of adaptation.
the Innovation Union is a space constituted by the performance of innovation and the performance of innovation is the performance of the researcher as an innovative researcher.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of critique in a context in which critique has been domesticated.
the ways in which the university is constituted as a site of innovation, with the implications of this for research practice, and with the possibilities for resistance.
the ways in which research is being reconstituted as an innovation and how this is changing the role of the researcher and the nature of research itself.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Innovation Union is a space constituted by devices for the measurement of innovation and actors acting in the names of such performance measures, which requires a reorientation to the present and the reconfiguration of a researcher’s attitude.
the Innovation Union, as a new regime of performance and a new mode of governing, has the potential to be a site of critique, and thus a site of resistance.
, in order to resist current regimes of performance, it is not enough for the researcher to be critical; she must be critical of the very conditions of her own criticality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EU has been reframed and reconstituted as an Innovation Union, which has implications for how we think about the role of the researcher and the university.
we have been able to show that the European Union is currently in the process of being reconfigured as an ‘innovation union’.
Hodgson’s chapter provides a very good overview of the current state of the EU’s Lisbon Strategy, the shift to innovation and the role of the researcher in the Innovation Union.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we must not be seduced by a discourse of ‘innovation’, but must instead seek to develop a discourse of ‘critique’.
there are two ways of understanding the university: as a space for the production of new knowledge and as an institution that produces and reproduces the conditions for the production of knowledge.
we need to think about how to make the university more than an entrepreneurial space, and how to think about the university as an innovative space.
